question: In the WOMAN trial of tranexamic acid for postpartum haemorrhage, how did the effect on death due to bleeding depend on the time from childbirth to treatment?
options: Tranexamic acid reduced death due to bleeding when given within 3 hours of childbirth, with no apparent reduction when given later.
Tranexamic acid reduced death due to bleeding only when given more than 3 hours after childbirth.
Tranexamic acid reduced death due to bleeding to the same extent regardless of treatment delay.
Tranexamic acid increased death due to bleeding when given within 3 hours of childbirth.
gold_answer: Tranexamic acid reduced death due to bleeding when given within 3 hours of childbirth, with no apparent reduction when given later.
notes: Every passage was checked against the PMC full text of PMC6891248 on 2026-11-19. Independent annotation and adjudication are required before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Tranexamic acid reduced death due to bleeding to the same extent regardless of treatment delay.

claims.text: In the WOMAN trial, tranexamic acid significantly reduced death due to bleeding (RR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.65–1.00; p = 0.045).

evidence.text: Tranexamic acid significantly reduced death due to bleeding (RR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.65–1.00; p = 0.045), with no increase in thromboembolic events or complications.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports a significant reduction in death due to bleeding with the same relative risk and confidence interval as the claim.

claims.text: In the WOMAN trial, tranexamic acid reduced death due to bleeding to the same extent when given more than 3 hours after childbirth.

evidence.text: When it was given beyond 3 h of childbirth, there was no apparent reduction in death due to bleeding (RR = 1.07, 95% CI 0.76–1.51; p = 0.70).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states there was no apparent reduction when treatment was given beyond 3 hours (RR 1.07), which refutes the claim of an equal reduction.

claims.text: The WOMAN trial showed that tranexamic acid reduced death due to bleeding more in women with moderate or severe anaemia.

evidence.text: The WOMAN-2 trial will assess the effectiveness of tranexamic acid for the prevention of post-partum haemorrhage in women with moderate or severe anaemia, which confers a considerably increased risk [29], [30].

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes a separate future prevention trial in women with anaemia; it reports no WOMAN result comparing effect by anaemia status, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
